title: Candidate-tree checks can miss entries added after enumeration
suggestion: Retain and recheck every traversed directory's identity and exact child-name set after hashing, both before and after activation, so additions, removals, and directory replacements invalidate the candidate tree.
rationale: installedCandidateTreeSha256 records only files returned by each initial readdirSync call. Its post-hash pass rechecks those known files, then checks only the package root inode; it never rechecks directory membership or nested-directory identities. A concurrent writer can add a file, including a nested node_modules package that changes module resolution, after its containing directory was enumerated during each validation pass. The digest still equals the catalog value and every current post-hash check succeeds, allowing unvalidated bytes into the activated profile. The existing race tests mutate already-enumerated files and do not cover an added entry.

title: Inherited template keys crash valid ordinary profile names
suggestion: Resolve shipped templates with an own-property check (or a null-prototype map/Map) before falling back to DEFAULT_PROFILE_BUNDLES, and use the same lookup in reconciliation and profile loading.
rationale: resolveProfileDir accepts names such as "toString", but PROFILE_TEMPLATES is a normal object and this direct lookup returns Object.prototype.toString instead of undefined. A fresh invocation of runPlugin("toString", ["list"]) reaches initProfile and throws "TypeError: bundles is not iterable" before pnpm runs. An already-created colliding profile can likewise fail in reconcilePlugins when its inherited value is passed to new Set, so valid ordinary profile names cannot be initialized or reconciled.
